reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 0

samples_reviewed.question_text: What is the place value of the digit 0 in 20?
What is the place value of the digit 1 in 15?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency wants subtraction taught by expressing minuend/subtrahend in expanded tens-and-ones form, but two of five samples ('What is the place value of the digit 0 in 20?', '...digit 1 in 15?') are not subtraction at all — they are the same digit-value questions as q2_2/q2_3, unrelated to the subtraction task.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: This node blends subtraction (12 combos) and place_value (8 combos) registries, but only 3 of 5 samples are actually subtraction, and none show the minuend or subtrahend explicitly decomposed into tens+ones notation in the visible text.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sample text stays short, e.g. 'What is 64 − 30?', within the word cap for Grade 1 Quarter 3.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Injecting unrelated place-value-digit questions into a subtraction-focused node (as also seen in q2_4) suggests the two combined DNAs are not yet fused into a single 'expanded-form subtraction' task, just alternating between two separate question types.

competency_alignment.rationale: Where subtraction is shown ('64 − 30 = 34'), it is a clean tens-only subtraction (no regrouping, consistent with the competency), but the expanded-form decomposition step itself, e.g. 60+4 minus 30+0, is never made visible in the text.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Minuends used (12, 20, 64) are 2-digit values consistent with the competency's tens-and-ones scope.
